Subject: Re: Draft dedicated commitment — timing questions

Irene / team,

Thanks for the initial term sheet. A few follow-ups from procurement as we model our FY28 budget: we need clearer timing on the tranche deliveries for Dedicated capacity (GPU hours / TPM equivalence) and how the prepay amortization works across fiscal years. Aurora prefers less ambiguity on invoice timing — we typically want most of the spend in FY28 (starts July 1), so we may push for front-loaded delivery or an accelerated year-1 tranche.

Specifically:
- Can you provide an explicit month-by-month delivery cadence for the first 12 months?
- For a 3-year multi-year prepay, how do you amortize the discount across invoices if our procurement team requires annual purchases?
- Any flexibility on a true-up mechanism at quarter boundaries?

Sending our PO template attached. Happy to hop on a 30-min call this week to align.

Thanks,
Lena Park
Head of Procurement, Aurora AI
ops@auroraai.com

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU tranche timing & amortization counterproposal — Aurora AI

Hi Lena — thanks for the note and the PO template. I pulled together two practical schedules and an amortization approach so your finance team can map spend to FYs. Attached: a spreadsheet (Aurora_Ramp_Schedule_v2.xlsx) and a redlined term sheet (redwood_term_sheet_Aurora_v3.pdf). Highlights below.

Option A (Balanced ramp, recommended for steady ops):
- Year 1 (months 0–12): 350 TPM-equivalent capacity (monthly smoothing available).
- Year 2 (months 13–24): 600 TPM-equivalent capacity.
- Year 3 (months 25–36): 900 TPM-equivalent capacity.
- Annual prepay discount: 15% for 3-year committed prepay paid at the start of each 12-mo period.

Option B (Front-loaded, procurement-friendly):
- Year 1: 600 TPM-equivalent (front-loaded to ensure early scale).
- Year 2: 500 TPM-equivalent.
- Year 3: 750 TPM-equivalent.
- Front-load credit amortization: we can amortize prepay across 12 months for accounting but allow you to consume credits faster if needed; unused credits carry forward within the same fiscal year, with a quarterly true-up.

Amortization / invoicing model we propose:
- Invoice issued at time of prepay (annual). Redwood posts the invoice to your account and amortizes the discount for reporting purposes over the 12-month window for that year.
- Quarterly true-up: any overage consumes prepaid credits first, under-usage is tracked and can be credited or moved to next quarter (limited carry-forward of up to 25% of that year's prepaid amount).
- Early termination / downgrade: standard pro-rata true-up minus a 10% early-termination fee unless you convert to a reduced committed baseline.

Operational asks / guarantees:
- We will commit to 95% availability for Dedicated pools tied to the tranche (detailed SLA in term sheet).
- 30% surge buffer available for the first 180 days of Year 1 to help with initial migrations (metered and drawn from prepay credits).

Next steps: Marcus and Ben are looped for pricing carve-outs and the DocuSign-ready term sheet is attached. If this looks ok in principle, we can share a DocuSign link and a final PO-ready term sheet.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com
(attachments: Aurora_Ramp_Schedule_v2.xlsx, redwood_term_sheet_Aurora_v3.pdf)
From: Lena Park <lena@auroraai.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU tranche timing & amortization counterproposal — Aurora AI

Irene / Marcus / Ben,

Appreciate the two options and the clear amortization language. Procurement likes Option B for front-loading but we have two follow-ups before we can present to finance: 1) confirmation that the 30% surge buffer is guaranteed capacity (not best-effort), and 2) more clarity on how the amortization appears on our P&L — will Redwood provide a quarterly statement showing consumed vs amortized credits that our accounting team can import?

Also FYI — our FY28 begins 2027-07-01. If we prepay for Year 1 before July, we need Redwood to allow the invoice to be dated in Q1 but the amortization to start on July 1 for our internal reporting. Is that workable?

If yes to both, we can move to an indicative signed term sheet next week and send a PO.

Thanks,
Lena
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena@auroraai.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU tranche timing & amortization counterproposal — Aurora AI

Lena — quick clarifications from our side:

1) Surge buffer: we can guarantee capacity for the 30% surge for the first 180 days by carving dedicated nodes in your pool and prioritizing routing for your customer id; we will include that as a guaranteed capacity carve in the term sheet (non-preemptible, subject to maintenance windows).

2) Accounting / statements: Redwood will provide a quarterly usage statement that shows: prepaid credits (starting balance), amortized amount for the quarter, credits consumed against usage, and remaining prepaid balance. We'll deliver this as a CSV export and a PDF summary — that should be importable into Aurora's ledger.

3) Invoice dating & amortization start: we can date the invoice at time of payment but set the amortization start to 2027-07-01 to match your FY. We will note this explicitly on the invoice and the quarterly statement.

4) Minor pricing ask: if Aurora can confirm a 3-year locked commit and sign within 14 days of the final term sheet, Redwood will extend the annual prepay discount from 15% to 17% (final redline in the attached term sheet).

Ben / Irene — please fold that into the DocuSign draft and we can send to Lena for signature + PO attachment.

Marcus Lin
Head of Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
